body:
Might be related to #115170.

#123614 aims to address that issue, but the current workaround is limited to Rogue GPUs, which (AFAIK) won't match the BXM-8-256.

If you are able to compile Godot from source, and can reproduce the crash reliably, we might be able to figure out how to make the workaround active on that GPU too.

CC @blueskythlikesclouds

> Might be related to [#115170](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/115170).
> 
> [#123614](https://github.com/godotengine/godot/pull/123614) aims to address that issue, but the current workaround is limited to Rogue GPUs, which (AFAIK) won't match the BXM-8-256.
> 
> If you are able to compile Godot from source, and can reproduce the crash reliably, we might be able to figure out how to make the workaround active on that GPU too.
> 

> CC [@blueskythlikesclouds](https://github.com/blueskythlikesclouds)

Backtrace attached: 7 crashes from one debugging session (Oct 2, 7:48-8:14 pm) in the editor while previewing materials in my animation project. All are SIGABRT from Scudo ("invalid chunk state when deallocating") on Godot worker threads. In every one, the free() is called from the same place in /vendor/lib64/hw/mt6855/vulkan.mtk.so (offset 0x163b34, frame no. 10 at 0x195074), called from libgodot_android.so. Infinix X6852, XOS 16, Vulkan driver 1.3.303. The same project worked on XOS 15 with 1.1.170.

[backtrace.txt](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/32960225/backtrace.txt)

> Might be related to https://github.com/godotengine/godot/issues/115170.

Seems to be completely separate. However, I'm suspecting it's another race condition since this appears to be a heap corruption?

>Seems to be completely separate. However, I'm suspecting it's another race condition since this appears to be a heap corruption?

I've noticed that making small changes to shader code can prevent the Material Preview crash, even when the overall functionality remains similar. The issue doesn't seem limited to a particular part of the shader, and the shaders still render correctly in the editor's actual 3D scene without any apparent issues. This makes me wonder whether the crash could be related to memory corruption or some issue with the editor's shader handling rather than the shader code itself. The earlier backtrace also suggested possible heap corruption, though I can't confirm the root cause yet.

(Edited for extra reply)
I also tested clearing Godot Editor Mobile's app data. This temporarily resolves the Material Preview crash, but the issue returns after interrupting the editor again. Small changes to the shader can also affect whether it crashes. Meanwhile, the shader continues to render correctly in the editor's actual 3D scene. This makes me suspect an issue involving the editor's internal state, shader handling, or rendering resources, although I haven't confirmed whether cache corruption is the cause.
